question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.B: To speed up medication administration during busy ward shifts
options.C: To ensure patients experience zero pain during every procedure
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

explanation: Injection safety encompasses protective measures for everyone involved in or affected by the injection process, preventing infections and injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is an injection considered a high-risk procedure despite its daily frequency?

options.A: It requires specialized surgical equipment to perform safely
options.B: It bypasses the body's natural skin barrier and enters sterile tissues directly
options.C: It is the only medical procedure that causes severe allergic reactions
options.D: It is always performed in emergency situations without preparation

explanation: Because a needle breaks the skin, any contamination on the equipment or technique introduces pathogens straight into the body, bypassing primary defenses. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: What happens if you use a single-dose medication vial for more than one patient?

options.A: It changes the chemical concentration of the prescribed drug
options.B: It transfers invisible pathogens between patients via contaminated equipment
options.C: It causes the remaining medicine to expire instantly
options.D: It increases the physical pain experienced during injection

explanation: Single-dose vials don't have preservatives. Reusing them lets germs multiply and spread infections to the next patient. Always use one vial per patient! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why should you never use both hands to recap a used needle?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes the injection painful
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.C: It violates hospital policies regarding medication waste disposal
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy medication round

explanation: Using two hands to recap makes it way too easy to miss the cap and puncture your own finger. Safety first—keep that hand away from the sharp end! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which virus is notorious for surviving on medical equipment and surfaces for days, making it very easy to spread if equipment is reused?
explanation: Hepatitis B is a tough survivor and can live on surfaces and tools outside the body for days. That's why strict sterilization and single-use rules are non-negotiable. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: A nurse changes a contaminated needle but reuses the plastic syringe barrel for another patient. What is the big danger here?

options.A: It causes an immediate allergic reaction in the patient
options.B: It transfers blood-borne pathogens trapped inside the barrel
options.C: It causes severe muscle necrosis at the injection site
options.D: It neutralizes the therapeutic effect of the injected drug

explanation: Remember, fluids and tiny amounts of blood pull back into the barrel during use. Changing just the needle isn't enough; the whole syringe must be single-use! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is a major complication if an intramuscular injection is given incorrectly in the buttocks?

options.B: Sciatic nerve injury leading to pain or paralysis
options.C: Immediate development of systemic respiratory failure
options.D: Complete blockage of the carotid artery

explanation: The sciatic nerve runs right through the lower, inner part of the buttock. This is why proper site landmarks (like the upper outer quadrant) are so crucial! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do unsterile injection techniques lead to painful abscesses?

options.A: By introducing bacteria from the skin surface deep into the muscle tissue
options.B: By causing an immediate chemical reaction that dissolves bone tissue
options.C: By increasing the local blood flow until the tissue swells and bursts
options.D: By freezing the surrounding muscle fibers and destroying blood vessels

explanation: When germs are pushed past the skin into warm muscle, they multiply, cause inflammation, and form pus (an abscess). Good antisepsis stops this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: What causes most needle-stick injuries among nursing students and staff?

options.C: Reading patient charts near the bedside

explanation: Recapping used needles is a leading cause of accidental pricks because a slip of the hand means a direct puncture. Never recap if you can avoid it! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are overfilled sharps containers dangerous on the ward?

options.A: They attract insects and rodents into patient care areas
options.B: They release toxic chemical fumes into the nursing station
options.C: They expose workers to protruding needles and unstable sharp items
options.D: They prevent the automated counting of used syringes

explanation: Once a sharps box is past its fill line, needles start stacking up near the top and can easily prick the next person trying to dispose of waste. Close them on time! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the single best way to stop infections from spreading in any healthcare setting?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns for every procedure

explanation: Simple handwashing or alcohol rubbing is your superpower against hospital infections. It removes germs picked up from patients and surroundings instantly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: How should you clean a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Wiping in a circular motion from the center outward and letting it dry
options.B: Applying an antiseptic spray and immediately inserting the needle
options.C: Wiping from the outer edges inward toward the center of the site
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth with a dry cotton ball

explanation: Always move from clean (center) to less clean (outward) to push germs away. Plus, letting the alcohol dry is what actually kills the microbes! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: If the hospital runs out of single-use syringes, what is the right way for a nurse to handle the situation?

options.A: By asking patients to purchase and bring their own needles from home
options.B: By skipping injections until the patient's condition improves naturally
options.C: By rinsing old syringes with hot water and reusing them for stable patients
options.D: By reporting the shortage and demanding proper supplies before performing injections

explanation: As a patient advocate, you must speak up and never compromise safety by taking shortcuts like equipment reuse. Patient safety comes first! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)

question: When caring for patients managing injections at home, what is a key duty for the nurse?

options.A: Disposing of patient sharps in regular household garbage bags
options.B: Instructing relatives to reuse syringes if they look clean
options.C: Teaching patients and families safe administration and disposal methods
options.D: Leaving used needles uncapped on the kitchen table for easy access

explanation: Great job! Educating patients and their families prevents accidental needle pricks in homes and communities after they leave the hospital. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)
